name: Elevation: The Harmon Voss Story
description: A corporate-commissioned biographical epic about Harmon Voss, the mythologized founder of HelioStruct Corponation, depicted rising from a Tier 2 fabrication floor to architect of the Spire's most iconic residential towers. The holographic presentation is deliberately grand — cathedral-scale projections designed for HelioStruct's public atrium spaces — with a sweeping orchestral score and a cast of thousands rendered via synthetic performance capture. Every HelioStruct employee was required to attend a screening during their orientation period from 2197 to 2209.
cultural_impact: The film's depiction of Tier 2 life as a noble proving ground rather than a trap became standard rhetoric in HelioStruct recruitment materials and influenced a generation of corporate mythology-building.
story_hooks: A physical film archive contains the unedited source interviews that prove Voss was a composite — someone wants those archives destroyed.
The synthetic performance capture artist who built the Voss composite is having a public breakdown and wants to confess.
A Tier 1 theater group performs an illegal parody version of the film verbatim but in the ruins of a building Voss allegedly built — which collapsed.
